weekSubtitle: Blends, Power Words, Nouns & Subject-Verb Match

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Blends with L, R, S
lessons.description: Learn 2- and 3-letter L, R, and S consonant blends, review spelling words, and play Sort it!
lessons.hint: Say each blend sound quickly together like a train: s-p-ace → space!

cards.frontHint: Two or three consonants that work together
cards.explanation: A blend is two consonants together (like pl in plum) or three consonants together (like str in strap). Say each sound quickly like a train!
cards.example: Two letters blend in plum, and three letters blend in strap!

cards.explanation: Two consonants blend together (p + l → pl).
cards.example: I ate a sweet purple plum for a snack.

cards.explanation: The second letter is L (g + l → gl).
cards.example: We found Egypt on the classroom globe.

cards.explanation: The second letter is L (p + l → pl).
cards.example: This park is a fun place to play.

cards.explanation: The second letter is L (g + l → gl).
cards.example: Birds glide smoothly through the sky.

cards.explanation: The second letter is L (c + l → cl).
cards.example: I use a clip to hold my paper.

cards.explanation: The second letter is L (p + l → pl).
cards.example: Plug the lamp cord into the wall.

cards.explanation: The second letter is L (f + l → fl).
cards.example: Our flag waves high in the breeze.

cards.explanation: The second letter is L (f + l → fl).
cards.example: The birthday candle has a warm flame.

cards.explanation: The second letter is L (s + l → sl).
cards.example: I ate a cheesy slice of pizza.

cards.explanation: Review spelling word! The second letter is L (s + l → sl).
cards.example: The playful puppy slid across the smooth floor.

cards.explanation: Review spelling word! The second letter is L (c + l → cl).
cards.example: Please close the classroom door gently.

cards.explanation: Review spelling word! The second letter is L (p + l → pl).
cards.example: Put the warm pancakes on a clean plate.

cards.explanation: A school mark. The second letter is R (g + r → gr).
cards.example: I got a great grade on my spelling work!

cards.explanation: Pull something along. The second letter is R (d + r → dr).
cards.example: Do not drag your backpack on the floor.

cards.explanation: The second letter is R (g + r → gr).
cards.example: Soft green grass grows in the yard.

cards.explanation: The second letter is R (g + r → gr). Hear each sound in grin!
cards.example: The happy boy gave a big grin.

cards.explanation: Review spelling word! The second letter is R (g + r → gr).
cards.example: One juicy purple grape rolled off the plate.

cards.explanation: thr = 3 letters in a blend! t + h + r sit together.
cards.example: The king sat on a shiny gold throne.

cards.explanation: Starts with S + p (sp).
cards.example: Astronauts travel far into space.

cards.explanation: Starts with S + w (sw).
cards.example: I can swim in the pool.

cards.explanation: Starts with S + k (sk).
cards.example: Sunscreen keeps your skin safe outside.

cards.explanation: Starts with S + n (sn).
cards.example: A long green snake slid through the grass.

cards.explanation: Starts with S + t (st).

cards.explanation: str = 3 consonants in a blend! s + t + r sit together.
cards.example: Buckle the red strap on your backpack.

cards.explanation: Ends with the -st blend (s + t).
cards.example: I studied hard for my spelling test.

cards.explanation: Ends with the -st blend (s + t).
cards.example: This is the last lap of the race!

cards.explanation: Ends with the -st blend (s + t).
cards.example: We just finished our homework!

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Power Words
lessons.description: Learn all 8 Power Words with meanings, examples, tips, and play Match it!
lessons.hint: Read the meaning and the example sentence to picture the word!

cards.explanation: A person who is very good at something; excellent, really good, or an expert.
cards.example: She is an ace at tennis.
cards.tip: It often means really good or the best!

cards.explanation: Wanting very much to do or have something; with great enthusiasm and excitement.
cards.example: He waited eagerly for the game.
cards.tip: When you really want something, you wait eagerly!

cards.explanation: A business or organization that provides a service and helps others.
cards.example: We asked a travel agency to plan our trip.
cards.tip: A place where people work together to help others.

cards.explanation: The making, buying, and selling of goods or services; an activity that makes money.
cards.example: Her family has a business.
cards.tip: Think of a shop or company where people buy and sell things!

cards.explanation: Sure of oneself and one's abilities; believing in yourself.
cards.example: He answered confidently.
cards.tip: It means without doubt — feeling sure you can do something well!

cards.explanation: Situated or placed in a particular spot or place.
cards.example: The school is located near the park.
cards.tip: Located tells you WHERE something is found!

cards.explanation: Something unknown or difficult to understand or explain.
cards.example: The story was a mystery.
cards.tip: It is something unknown that needs clues to solve!

cards.explanation: Flows or leaks slowly through small holes — the opposite of pours out!
cards.example: Water seeps from the wall.
cards.tip: Not a big splash—just slow drops little by little, the opposite of pours out.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Singular & Plural Nouns
lessons.description: Learn ONE vs MORE THAN ONE nouns, all 10 poster pairs, and play Add -s or -es?
lessons.hint: Look at the end of the word: s, x, ch, sh → add -es!

cards.explanation: A noun names a person, place, animal or thing.
cards.example: Our teacher read a book about a cat at the park.

cards.frontHint: ONE (cat, book, girl) vs MORE THAN ONE (cats, books, girls)
cards.explanation: Singular = ONE person, place, animal or thing (cat, book, girl, apple). Plural = MORE THAN ONE (cats, books, girls, apples).
cards.example: One cat sleeps, and three cats play.

cards.explanation: Just put -s at the end to make most nouns plural!
cards.example: Two dogs sit under the tall trees.
examples: cat 🐱 → cats 🐱🐱🐱  •  apple 🍎 → apples 🍎🍎
book 📘 → books 📚  •  girl 👧 → girls 👧👧
dog 🐶 → dogs 🐶🐶  •  chair 🪑 → chairs 🪑🪑
tree 🌳 → trees 🌳🌳🌳  •  globe 🌍 → globes 🌍🌍

cards.frontTitle: Rule 2: Ends in s, x, ch, sh → add -es
cards.frontHint: Add -es so words are easy to say
cards.backTitle: Nouns ending in s, x, ch, sh
cards.explanation: Nouns ending in s, x, ch, sh → add -es so they are easy to say!
cards.example: Two buses stop by the big boxes.
examples: bus 🚌 → buses 🚌🚌  •  glass 🥛 → glasses 🥛🥛
box 📦 → boxes 📦📦  •  fox 🦊 → foxes 🦊🦊
watch ⌚ → watches ⌚⌚  •  brush 🪥 → brushes 🪥🪥

activity.title: Add -s or -es?
activity.instruction: Tap the correct plural for all 10 nouns!

items.explanation: Bus ends in s → add -es: buses!
Box ends in x → add -es: boxes!
Watch ends in ch → add -es: watches!
Brush ends in sh → add -es: brushes!
Glass ends in s → add -es: glasses!

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Subject-Verb Agreement
lessons.description: Make the subject and verb match in present tense and play Fix the sentence!
lessons.hint: He, She, It — the -s must fit! I, You, We, They — no -s, hooray!

cards.explanation: The correct verb form depends on the subject. Think of a see-saw in the NOW tense (present): one subject adds -s, more than one has no -s!
cards.example: The teacher sits, and the teachers sit.

cards.explanation: In a sentence that tells about now, one person or thing (singular) uses a verb that ends in -s.
cards.example: Greta looks for her backpack.
examples: The teacher sits in the desk chair. 🪑
The student sits in the classroom. 🏫
Greta looks for her backpack. 🎒
Dwayne jumps to catch the ball. ⚽

cards.explanation: In a sentence that tells about now, plural subjects (more than one) use a verb without -s!
cards.example: Stars light up the sky.
examples: The teachers sit in the desk chairs. 🪑
Plants and trees grow in the forest. 🌲
My friends run to catch the bus. 🚌
Stars light up the sky. ✨

cards.frontTitle: Ends in s, sh, ch, tch, z, x → add -es
cards.explanation: Verbs ending in -s, -sh, -ch, -tch, -z, or -x add -es to match a singular subject:
cards.example: The train passes and the boy reaches.
examples: The train passes → The trains pass 🚂
The girl watches → The girls watch ⛸️
The chef mixes → The chefs mix 🍲
A fly buzzes • The dart misses • Mom washes

cards.explanation: If the pronoun he, she, or it is the subject in the present tense, always add -s or -es to the verb!
cards.example: He throws and she catches the ball.
examples: He throws the ball. ⚾  •  She catches the ball. 🧤
He washes the car. 🚗  •  She picks a movie. 🎬
It seems later than six o'clock. ⏰

cards.explanation: If the pronoun I, you, we, or they is the subject in the present tense, do NOT add -s or -es!
cards.example: They watch the game and we cheer.
examples: I reach for the ticket. 🎟️  •  I eat breakfast. 🥣
You tell the truth. 💬  •  They cheer when we score. 🎉
We cheer very loudly. 📣  •  They sit on chairs. 🪑

cards.explanation: He, She, It — the -s must fit!
cards.example: He, She, It — the -s must fit! I, You, We, They — no -s, hooray!

activity.title: Fix the sentence!
activity.instruction: Read the wrong sentence, then tap the fixed one!

items.explanation: Harlan is ONE person and fix ends in x → add -es: fixes!

items.wrongSentence: A fly buzz by my ear.
options: A fly buzzes by my ear.
A fly buzzs by my ear.
A fly buzzing by my ear.
items.answer: A fly buzzes by my ear.
items.explanation: A fly is ONE thing and buzz ends in z → add -es: buzzes!

items.wrongSentence: Coach Carr teach us how to throw.
options: Coach Carr teaches us how to throw.
Coach Carr teachs us how to throw.
Coach Carr teaching us how to throw.
items.answer: Coach Carr teaches us how to throw.
items.explanation: Coach Carr is ONE person and teach ends in ch → add -es: teaches!
The dart is ONE thing and miss ends in s → add -es: misses!
Mom is ONE person and wash ends in sh → add -es: washes!
I, You, We, They — no -s, hooray! We laugh at the joke.
I, You, We, They — no -s, hooray! I know the best shortcut.
